findings: 1. Two live websites are splitting the brand, the SEO and the ad traffic. On 14 Sep 2026 both solaruniverseindia.com and solaruniverse.co.in load, both are indexed, and both present themselves as the official Solar Universe India site. They do not agree. The legacy site says "With an experience of over 10 years"; the new site says "Established in 2003" (23 years). The legacy site claims "offices in Kenya, Tanzania, Ethiopia and Ireland" and "export to more than 25 partners"; the new site never mentions the international arm and instead leads with "8MW of solar rooftop systems... 27 states... 75 channel partners" and "650+ projects installed in 27 states". A buyer who clicks an ad, then Googles the brand, lands on a different company. Every backlink, review citation and ad click is being divided between two domains, so neither accumulates authority.

2. There is a Lorem Ipsum block sitting in the live testimonial carousel. On solaruniverse.co.in, under the name Ashok Nehru (who also appears as the J&K regional partner on the same page), the testimonial text reads "Lorem Ipsum is simply dummy text of the printing and typesetting industry..." in full, through to "Aldus PageMaker". The same carousel reuses one identical stock avatar image for every reviewer. And the lead testimonial from Anil Chaturvedi is not a customer review at all - it reads "the best platform to grow your carrier... Happy to become the part of Solar Universe India (SUI)", which is an employee review, complete with the typo, presented as customer proof. This is the first thing a Rs.2 lakh rooftop buyer reads.

3. Zero PM Surya Ghar content anywhere in the funnel - in the middle of the biggest subsidy wave India has had. Neither domain has a subsidy page, a slab table, or a single mention of the scheme. As of Aug-Sep 2026 PM Surya Ghar has crossed 50.06 lakh households and 16,185 MW, is running at 16,328 installs a day (up from 5,038/day in Oct 2025), has disbursed Rs.28,024 crore in DBT, and has 34,219 registered vendors competing for exactly these leads. Residential buyers now open with "how much subsidy do I get?" The correct answer - Rs.30,000 for 1 kW, Rs.60,000 for 2 kW, Rs.78,000 for 3 kW and above, DCR and ALMM modules mandatory - is the single highest-converting block a residential solar page can carry, and it is absent.

4. The Day-1 leak is confirmed, and it is worse than it looked: the pricing exists, it is just kept away from the ads. SUI publishes live, transactable prices on third-party marketplaces - Rs.2,149 for the 5W home lighting set, Rs.2,979 for the 60W DC set, Rs.3,129 for the 200VA off-grid inverter, Rs.45,249-48,657 for the 200W pump-and-panel combo. The owned funnel shows none of it. There is no bundle price for panel + inverter + battery, no kW-wise rooftop price, no EMI option, no finance partner. The ad promises savings and then asks for a phone number before the buyer knows whether this is a Rs.3,000 purchase or a Rs.3 lakh one. That mismatch is what inflates cost-per-qualified-lead.

5. The WhatsApp link on the new site is built wrong and will fail for a share of users. Both CTA buttons point to wa.me/9810288787 - a 10-digit number with no 91 country code. WhatsApp's click-to-chat spec requires the full international number; without it the link resolves unreliably and can throw "phone number shared via url is invalid". On top of that the funnel offers three competing contact routes (Customer Care 9212030030, Trade Inquiries 9810288787, and the WhatsApp link), so even the clicks that do land cannot be attributed back to a creative.

6. The legacy site is visibly decaying and it is still taking ad traffic. Live on 14 Sep 2026: the product grid is headed "SOLAR PORDUCTS" and "HOT SAILING PRODUCTS" (both typos); six of those product tiles - Solar Inverters/PCU, SUI-Lite PC, Solar LED Lighting, Solar Street Lighting, On & Off Grid Inverter, Solar Fencing - link to # and go nowhere; the Uttarakhand 28KWP star project links to #; the "DISCOVER MORE" and "EXPLORE MORE" buttons loop back to the homepage; the Facebook/Twitter embed renders the literal error string "Rate limit exceeded"; and the "Get Directions" link points at an old contact_us.html URL from a pre-WordPress site. Every uploaded image on the page is dated 2021-12. Real assets are stranded behind that decay - RBI Estate Department (20 kWp, Rajasthan), Islamiya University J&K (500 kW), JIIMS University Delhi (80 kW), Mahaveer/Gannaur poultry farm Sonipat (122 kWp) - institutional logos most Delhi competitors cannot match, and none of them are in the creatives.

7. Proof and ratings are inconsistent across the places buyers actually check. Justdial shows 4.3 from 18 ratings and "22 Years in Business"; IndiaMART shows the parent Success Impex Pvt Ltd at 3.8-4.0 from 74-79 ratings; Moglix panel reviews average 4.3; but the Amazon brand store tells a different story - the 200VA off-grid inverter sits at 2.7 from 11 reviews, the 200W DC-AC converter at 2.0, and large parts of the Amazon store read "Currently unavailable". The founding year also changes by source: 2003 on both sites, "22 years" on Justdial, and 1994 on TradeIndia for the parent. The ads claim quality; the marketplaces a buyer checks in the next thirty seconds do not consistently back it.
